definition: A business model where companies compete for users' time and attention, monetizing it through advertising and data collection to maximize engagement and profits.
metaDescription: Learn about the attention economy - how platforms profit from capturing your time and attention through data collection and targeted advertising.
simpleExplanation: The attention economy treats your focus as a valuable resource. Social media platforms, websites, and apps use algorithms, notifications, and engaging content to keep you online longer, then sell your attention to advertisers.
whyItMatters: This model incentivizes platforms to collect extensive personal data and use persuasive design techniques that can impact mental health, privacy, and your ability to control your own time and focus.
technicalDetail: Companies deploy sophisticated algorithms that analyze user behavior patterns, engagement metrics, and personal data to optimize content delivery. They use A/B testing, machine learning models, and psychological techniques to maximize time-on-platform and ad revenue.

examples.explanation: Platforms like Facebook and Instagram use endless scrolling, personalized content, and push notifications to keep users engaged for hours, then display targeted ads based on collected data.
Mobile games use daily rewards, limited-time events, and social features to maintain daily engagement, while collecting data on player behavior to optimize monetization strategies.
YouTube's recommendation algorithm analyzes viewing history and engagement to suggest videos that maximize watch time, keeping users on the platform longer to see more ads.
